claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is controlled by the degree of chemical short-range order.
Chemical short-range order drives formation of a duplex microstructure containing ordered domains in a disordered matrix.
The ordered domains in the proposed duplex structure are nanoscale and B2-like.
An ordered/disordered duplex structure can promote high-temperature strength while retaining ductility.
Ordered/disordered interfaces improve radiation tolerance by trapping radiation-induced defects.
A ductile disordered matrix preserves cryogenic toughness.
An as-cast or homogenized Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy can have a largely random or mixed-phase initial microstructure with minimal short-range order.
Aging at 600–800 °C can induce and tune short-range order and the volume fraction of ordered phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni.
Rapid quenching produces a predominantly random Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni structure with minimal short-range order.
Short-range order creates additional barriers to dislocation motion, including locking associated with local ordering.
The short-range-order-induced barriers enhance high-temperature yield strength.
Ordered/disordered interfaces help distribute strain under cryogenic conditions.
Ordering reduces deleterious diffusion processes and thereby improves environmental resistance.
An ordered-domain fraction of approximately 30–50% will increase high-temperature yield strength by roughly 10–20% relative to a rapidly quenched baseline.
A moderate ordered-domain fraction will improve radiation-damage resistance relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
A moderate ordered-domain fraction will enhance environmental resistance without significantly reducing cryogenic toughness.
Al must be present in sufficient quantity to promote B2 ordering, but excessive Al may overwhelm the desired duplex microstructure.
The relationship between short-range order and the combined properties may depend sensitively on aging schedule and initial microstructure.

contradictions.description: The quenched/reference state is described variously as having minimal SRO, being predominantly random, and being fully disordered. Minimal SRO is not strictly equivalent to complete disorder.
